title: NYC DOT AV testing permit
summary: New York City requires AV testers to hold a New York State DMV demonstration permit and then a separate NYC DOT testing permit, with a $5,000 annual fee and a test operator present and ready to take control. NYC DOT reviews the technology, testing plan and operator training; for-hire services must also follow Taxi and Limousine Commission licensing rules.

title: Seattle AV testing permit
summary: Seattle requires a Street Use permit for autonomous vehicle testing, with a human driver ready to take control, proof of insurance, first-responder information for the fire and police departments, advance notice of tests, and reporting of collisions and violations. Zoox and NVIDIA hold permits issued in 2023; other developers need none because their testing is manual data collection or Level 2 assistance.

title: State-led passenger service oversight
summary: California's DMV permits AV testing and deployment, and the CPUC permits passenger service, which requires an underlying DMV permit. The SFMTA states that it does not issue AV permits and that San Francisco has no permitting authority over AVs on city streets; it works with state and federal regulators and takes public feedback.

title: Market Street pickup and drop-off access
summary: On April 10, 2025, at Mayor Lurie's direction, San Francisco began allowing Waymo autonomous vehicles to pick up and drop off passengers on Market Street, where transit, paratransit, taxis and emergency vehicles were already authorized. SFMTA said taxi access would not change; its notice gives no hours, locations or conditions for Waymo.

title: AV coordination under Texas preemption
summary: Texas law bars cities from regulating automated motor vehicle operation, and under SB 2807 the state DMV authorizes Level 4 and 5 operations, so Austin issues no AV operating authorization. The city keeps a weekly, unvalidated dashboard of AV incidents reported to it, directs residents to 9-1-1 for dangerous situations and 3-1-1 otherwise, and passes safety information to operators.

title: Boston AV testing approach
summary: Boston uses a phased approach in which companies sign a memorandum of agreement with the city, test with safety drivers, and are limited in early phases to good weather and daylight. The city first approved Motional (then nuTonomy) for on-street testing in December 2016; Motional's listed approval ran through January 2024, so the page may not reflect current status.
